findings.claim: The rear-edge warrant carries a WEB translation-punctuation fact as corroboration, which the marker policy bars at any weight.
findings.grounds: The rationale states that the English quotation closes at web:Isa.27.5 and calls it 'a translation-punctuation boundary carried here as non-driving corroboration alone'. web:Isa.27.5 ends with a closing curly double quote opened at web:Isa.27.2; that quotation span is WEB editorial punctuation (tier-4), and MT carries none of it — the row's own closing verse reads בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא כֶּ֥רֶם חֶ֖מֶד עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) at the row's opening verse, and the row's closing verse ends שָׁל֖וֹם יַֽעֲשֶׂה לִּֽי (oshb:Isa.27.5, byte tier) with no quotation apparatus of any kind. Tier-4 metadata is never boundary evidence and never corroboration; labelling it 'non-driving' does not license carrying it in the warrant.
findings.proposed_change: Strike the web:Isa.27.5 translation-punctuation sentence from boundary_rationale and let the rear edge stand on the oshb:Isa.27.6 onset alone; drop web:Isa.27.5 from boundary_evidence_refs if no non-tier-4 claim remains attached to it.

findings.claim: 'the book's one instance of a dedicated song-announcement formula' is an unswept uniqueness claim and is contradicted by the bytes at two further sites.
findings.grounds: The clause carries no digit-bearing sweep citation and names no swept object ('a dedicated song-announcement formula' is not a defined count object). Byte counterevidence: אָשִׁ֤ירָה נָּא֙ לִֽידִידִ֔י שִׁירַ֥ת דּוֹדִ֖י (oshb:Isa.5.1, byte tier) and שִׁ֤ירוּ לַֽיהוָה֙ שִׁ֣יר חָדָ֔שׁ (oshb:Isa.42.10, byte tier) are both first-person/imperative song announcements; the shir skeleton stands at 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses; oshb:Isa.3.19, oshb:Isa.5.1, oshb:Isa.23.15, oshb:Isa.23.16, oshb:Isa.24.9, oshb:Isa.26.1, oshb:Isa.30.29, oshb:Isa.42.10, oshb:Isa.53.9), a substring object that itself blends the necklace and rich-man tokens. The claim escaped the universals gate twice: 'one instance' is outside that detector's lexicon, and the sentence names a tier beside a ref, which trips its tier-vocabulary dampener.
findings.proposed_change: Replace with a swept, object-named statement (e.g. name the koh-yushar formula at יוּשַׁ֥ר הַשִּׁיר (oshb:Isa.26.1, byte tier) as ONE attested song-announcement form, with its digit), or delete the uniqueness clause; the construal disclaimer about the row's own verse stands without it.

findings.claim: The rear edge is argued as an address to Jacob and Israel; oshb:Isa.27.6 carries no address at all — it is third-person predication.
findings.grounds: The rationale reads that oshb:Isa.27.6 is 'addressing Jacob and Israel by name rather than continuing the vineyard's second-person/first-person address'. The verse's own bytes are הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב יָצִ֥יץ וּפָרַ֖ח יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier): no vocative particle, no second-person form, the names standing as third-person subjects of third-masculine-singular verbs. The contrast term is also mis-set: inside oshb:Isa.27.2-Isa.27.5 the vineyard is never addressed in the second person either — it is carried by third-feminine-singular suffixes (אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ, oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier), while the one second-person form is the plural imperative עַנּוּ לָֽהּ (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) addressed to an unnamed audience. The seam survives on a corrected warrant (referent/scene shift), but the stated form-class ground does not.
findings.proposed_change: Restate the rear-edge ground as a referent/scene shift — oshb:Isa.27.6 names Jacob and Israel as third-person subjects where oshb:Isa.27.2-Isa.27.5 carried a third-feminine-singular vineyard referent — and drop the word 'address' from both halves of the contrast.

findings.claim: The English gloss at web:Isa.27.3 runs two Hebrew words past the splice it is paired with.
findings.grounds: The row pairs אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ (oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier) with the curly-quoted run 'I, Yahweh, am its keeper. I will water it every moment' (web:Isa.27.3); the second English clause renders לִרְגָעִ֖ים אַשְׁקֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier), which is outside the splice. The WEB run itself re-checks verbatim against the staged WEB text; the defect is extent parity only.
findings.proposed_change: Either extend the splice to אֲנִ֤י יְהוָה֙ נֹֽצְרָ֔הּ לִרְגָעִ֖ים אַשְׁקֶ֑נָּה (oshb:Isa.27.3, byte tier) or cut the gloss back to 'I, Yahweh, am its keeper.'

findings.claim: confidence 'high' with frontier_flag_considered false does not survive the row's own concessions at either edge.
findings.grounds: Front edge: the row's onset בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) does not distinguish oshb:Isa.27.2 from oshb:Isa.27.1, whose own onset בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) matches it at accent_stripped tier; the row itself downgrades the song frame to 'a construal, not a named frame class', leaving a tier-3 setumah after oshb:Isa.27.1 as the front-edge corroboration. Rear edge: one tier-4 element (finding 1) and a byte-false form ground (finding 3). The parashah layer's own segment additionally runs from after oshb:Isa.27.1 to after oshb:Isa.27.6, so the tier-3 layer straddles this row's rear seam rather than supporting it.
findings.proposed_change: Lower confidence to medium and set frontier_flag_considered true, or re-argue the front edge from the second-person plural imperative in oshb:Isa.27.2's own bytes as the distinguishing tier-1 signal.

findings.claim: The rear-edge warrant asserts a Hebrew frame onset at Isa.27.12 with no pointed splice, no tier label, and no oshb ref.
findings.grounds: The closing sentence reads 'Isa.27.12 opens its own ba-yom-hahu formula, a fresh frame this row does not share' — a transliteration, argued only from a web: ref (boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.27.12 and no oshb:Isa.27.12). The verse's own bytes are וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) — the waw-prefixed long form, which the neighbouring rows themselves distinguish from the bare form; the claim is true but is left resting on the rendering. Pointed splices with tier labels are mandatory for every boundary-relevant Hebrew claim.
findings.proposed_change: Splice וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) into the closing sentence, name the long form, and add oshb:Isa.27.12 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: The front-edge warrant names no ruled tier-1 signal standing in oshb:Isa.27.6's own bytes.
findings.grounds: The row opens on הַבָּאִים֙ יַשְׁרֵ֣שׁ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) and states, correctly, that the participle supplies no noun of its own and that the dating sense is the rendering's contribution — so the onset is expressly NOT a dated frame formula. What is left unnamed is the signal that does open the unit: the referent turn to the third-person subjects יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב and יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Isa.27.6, byte tier) after the vineyard's third-feminine-singular referent. The parashah layer gives no front-seam corroboration either — its mark falls after oshb:Isa.27.6, inside this span, not before it. confidence medium_low with frontier_flag_considered true already registers the thinness honestly.
findings.proposed_change: Name the referent/scene shift explicitly as the front-edge tier-1 ground, or record in device_notes that the front edge is argued from continuity of subject rather than from a frame onset.

findings.claim: The English gloss at web:Isa.27.12 runs five Hebrew words past the splice it is paired with.
findings.grounds: The row pairs וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא יַחְבֹּ֧ט יְהוָ֛ה (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) with 'It will happen in that day that Yahweh will thresh from the flowing stream of the Euphrates to the brook of Egypt' (web:Isa.27.12); the 'from the flowing stream ... to the brook of Egypt' clause renders מִשִּׁבֹּ֥לֶת הַנָּהָ֖ר עַד נַ֣חַל מִצְרָ֑יִם (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier), outside the splice. The WEB run is verbatim; the defect is extent parity only. The row's digits re-derive exactly: the waw-prefixed long form stands at 13 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 13 verses), and the two onsets וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) and וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier) do agree only at accent_stripped tier, as claimed.
findings.proposed_change: Either extend the splice through מִשִּׁבֹּ֥לֶת הַנָּהָ֖ר עַד נַ֣חַל מִצְרָ֑יִם (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) or cut the gloss at 'that Yahweh will thresh'.

findings.claim: The setumah recorded after MT 27:12 is given as one of two reasons the merge rival is set aside while the same sentence labels it non-driving.
findings.grounds: The rejected-alternative's second sentence sets the rival aside 'because both halves are complete on their own terms and the mark, however weak, falls exactly at the image change' — the parashah mark is a conjunct of the stated reason, though the same sentence labels it '(tier-3, non-driving)'. The mark is real and correctly typed (pmarks_Isa.json records SAMEKH at Isa.27.12, single-witness) and the seam has an independent byte ground — each verse opens its own frame onset, וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) against וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier) — so the finding is the weighting, not the mark.
findings.proposed_change: Recast the second sentence so the rival is set aside on the two independent frame onsets, with the setumah named after the fact as tier-3 corroboration rather than inside the 'because' clause.

findings.claim: The row's close is corroborated by its own parent-frame boundary, which is campaign architecture and cannot corroborate anything about this row's edge.
findings.grounds: The rationale states 'The verse is the closing verse of its book-level parent grouping, which corroborates this row's own close', after opening with the same fact ('The closing verse of the book-level parent grouping opens with...'). parent_collection is 'M2 Isa.13.1-Isa.27.13' and rows never straddle a frame seam by rule, so every row ending the frame necessarily ends at Isa.27.13 — the corroboration is entailed by the architecture, not observed in the text. The genuine byte ground is stated separately and holds: oshb:Isa.28.1 opens verse-initially on ה֗וֹי (oshb:Isa.28.1, byte tier).
findings.proposed_change: Delete the corroboration clause and the duplicated parent-frame sentence; leave the close carried by the oshb:Isa.28.1 hoy onset.

findings.claim: The same contested seam is registered as a weighed frontier rival by the neighbour row and as settled here: confidence high, frontier_flag_considered false.
findings.grounds: This row's front edge is the Isa.27.12|Isa.27.13 seam. The neighbour argues that seam at confidence medium with frontier_flag_considered true, and its rejected-alternative weighs a merge because both verses open the same formula, agreeing only at accent_stripped tier — וְהָיָה֙ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא (oshb:Isa.27.12, byte tier) against וְהָיָ֣ה בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.27.13, byte tier). This row's own front-edge ground is 'its own repetition of the day-formula', which is precisely the shared feature, plus a tier-3 setumah; a repetition of the neighbour's own onset cannot separate the two verses on its own. The rear edge (oshb:Isa.28.1 hoy) is strong, but the front edge cannot be more settled here than next door.
findings.proposed_change: Set confidence to medium and frontier_flag_considered true, matching the neighbour's registration of the shared seam; or state the independent front-edge ground (each verse a complete proclamation with its own image) instead of the shared formula.

findings.claim: 'no mark in the inventory follows Isa.27.13 itself' does not name which inventory, and a seg IS recorded at MT 27:13 in another disclosure layer.
findings.grounds: The parashah layer is indeed silent at Isa.27.13 (pmarks_Isa.json marks: SAMEKH at Isa.27.12, nothing at Isa.27.13), so the claim is true of that layer. But the paseq inventory records 1 seg at Isa.27.13 (single-witness, count-only), and the row's own closing verse therefore carries a recorded disclosure object that the blanket negative reads as denying.
findings.proposed_change: Qualify the sentence to 'no parashah mark follows Isa.27.13', or disclose the count-only paseq seg at MT 27:13 (single-witness) alongside it.

findings.claim: The rival's day-formula is called 'the same bare verse-initial formula' as at Isa.27.1 and Isa.27.2 with no tier named; it is not the same at byte tier.
findings.grounds: The rejected alternative splices בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier) and then asserts sameness with Isa.27.1 and Isa.27.2 without a tier label. Collated: that run reaches only accent_stripped tier against oshb:Isa.27.1 and against oshb:Isa.27.2 — the three onsets בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא (oshb:Isa.28.5, byte tier), בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֡וּא (oshb:Isa.27.1, byte tier) and בַּיּ֖וֹם הַה֑וּא (oshb:Isa.27.2, byte tier) differ from one another in their accents. Every other recurrence claim in this row is tier-labelled (the crown-noun echo is correctly given at accent_stripped tier, and its digits re-derive exactly: 3 sites in the chapter and 4 book-wide at skeleton tier — oshb:Isa.28.1, oshb:Isa.28.3, oshb:Isa.28.5, oshb:Isa.62.3).
findings.proposed_change: Add the tier to the sameness claim: 'the same bare verse-initial formula ... at accent_stripped tier'.

findings.claim: The rear-edge warrant asserts an imperative address and a fresh addressee at Isa.28.14 with no pointed splice and no oshb ref.
findings.grounds: The closing clause reads 'the verse just before the imperative address that opens a fresh addressee at web:Isa.28.14'; boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.28.14 only. The verse's own bytes are לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier) — imperative plus vocative, so the claim is true, but the row's own closing warrant is left resting on the WEB rendering. The strongest division mark in the region does fall at this seam and IS disclosed (pmarks_Isa.json: PE at Isa.28.13, cited as petuchah, single-witness, correctly not conflated with SAMEKH) — but tier-3 cannot carry a rear edge either.
findings.proposed_change: Splice לָכֵ֛ן שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אַנְשֵׁ֣י לָצ֑וֹן (oshb:Isa.28.14, byte tier) into the closing sentence and add oshb:Isa.28.14 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: The '5 verses book-wide' digit does not belong to the summons form the sentence points at; that form stands at 1 verse.
findings.grounds: The sentence's antecedent is the quoted four-imperative run הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier): 'That summons form alone does not fix the unit's type: it stands at 5 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 5 verses)'. Re-swept at skeleton tier: the full run stands at 1 verse (oshb:Isa.28.23); its two-word head stands at 1 verse (oshb:Isa.28.23). The figure 5 is the count for the single token הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier) — 5 verses (oshb:Isa.1.10, oshb:Isa.8.9, oshb:Isa.28.23, oshb:Isa.51.4, oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4) — an object the sentence never names. That substring object also blends speech classes at the form level, not only at the 'openings of different speech classes' the row means: the MT 64:3 (= WEB 64:4) site is the perfect לֹ֣א (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier), not an imperative at all.
findings.proposed_change: Name the swept object before the digit — e.g. 'the single imperative הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier) stands at 5 verses book-wide at skeleton tier (sweep: 5 verses), one site carrying a perfect rather than an imperative' — or replace the digit with the count for the run actually quoted (1 verse).

findings.claim: The rear-edge warrant asserts a hoy onset at Isa.29.1 with no pointed splice and no oshb ref.
findings.grounds: The closing clause reads 'before the next hoy onset at web:Isa.29.1'; boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.29.1 and no oshb:Isa.29.1. The verse's own bytes are ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.29.1, byte tier), verse-initial — the claim is true and is a ruled tier-1 signal, but the row leaves its own rear edge argued from a transliteration over a web: ref.
findings.proposed_change: Splice ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.29.1, byte tier) into the closing sentence and add oshb:Isa.29.1 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: A chapter-division fact is carried inside the closing warrant without a non-evidential label.
findings.grounds: The rationale closes 'the chapter's own closing verse, before the next hoy onset at web:Isa.29.1'. Chapter divisions are tier-4 and are never boundary evidence or corroboration; the row's real closing ground (the oshb:Isa.29.1 onset) sits in the same clause, so the tier-4 element reads as co-supporting it. Contrast this row's neighbour-facing practice elsewhere in the batch, where a tier-4 element is at least explicitly labelled non-driving.
findings.proposed_change: Delete 'the chapter's own closing verse' from boundary_rationale, or mark it explicitly as a locator carrying no evidential weight.

findings.claim: device_notes cites the governing vocabulary rule as authority in row prose.
findings.grounds: The disclosure opens 'Operative-category deviation disclosed here per the closed vocabulary's own rule: trial_speech is staged for the 40-48 disputation neighbourhoods...'. The deviation disclosure itself is mandated and its substance is sound — the row's own bytes carry a summons-to-attention opening, הַאֲזִ֥ינוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ קוֹלִ֑י הַקְשִׁ֥יבוּ וְשִׁמְע֖וּ (oshb:Isa.28.23, byte tier), with the in-span verse-initial interrogatives הֲכֹ֣ל (oshb:Isa.28.24, byte tier) and הֲלוֹא֙ (oshb:Isa.28.25, byte tier) carrying the disputation reading. The register purge is what the rule-citation phrasing trips.
findings.proposed_change: Restate without the governance citation, e.g. 'trial_speech is applied here on formal grounds: the row's own bytes carry the summons-to-attention opening and two verse-initial interrogatives, though the farmer parable sits outside the disputation neighbourhoods.'

findings.claim: The cross-seam of-hosts recurrence is asserted between two runs that match at NO tier; only the shorter phrase inside them matches.
findings.grounds: device_notes states that מֵעִ֨ם יְהוָ֤ה צְבָאוֹת֙ תִּפָּקֵ֔ד (oshb:Isa.29.6, byte tier) 'meets' מֵעִ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת (oshb:Isa.28.29, byte tier) 'only at accent-stripped tier'. Collated as quoted, the oshb:Isa.29.6 run reaches tier 'none' against oshb:Isa.28.29 — it carries a fourth word that is absent there. What is true is the claim about the three-word phrase: מֵעִ֛ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת (oshb:Isa.28.29, byte tier) stands at 1 verse at byte tier and 3 verses at accent_stripped tier (sweep: 3 verses — oshb:Isa.8.18, oshb:Isa.28.29, oshb:Isa.29.6), so the row's digit is right while its quoted comparison is not.
findings.proposed_change: Cut the oshb:Isa.29.6 splice back to its first three words so the two quoted runs are the same phrase, and keep the accent_stripped tier label and the 3-verse digit as they stand.

findings.claim: The rear-edge warrant asserts a fresh imperative onset at Isa.29.9 with no pointed splice and no oshb ref.
findings.grounds: The closing clause reads 'the verse just before the fresh imperative onset at web:Isa.29.9'; boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.29.9 only. The verse's own bytes are הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ (oshb:Isa.29.9, byte tier) — the claim is true, but the row's rear edge is argued from the rendering. The row's in-span digits by contrast all re-derive exactly: the name-chain stands at 3 verses / 5 token occurrences at skeleton tier (sweep: 3 verses — oshb:Isa.29.1, oshb:Isa.29.2, oshb:Isa.29.7), and the shared run holds at byte tier across exactly 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses — oshb:Isa.29.7, oshb:Isa.29.8).
findings.proposed_change: Splice הִתְמַהְמְה֣וּ וּתְמָ֔הוּ הִשְׁתַּֽעַשְׁע֖וּ וָשֹׁ֑עוּ (oshb:Isa.29.9, byte tier) into the closing sentence and add oshb:Isa.29.9 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: Two parashah-mark claims are cited under a web: prefix, though the layer is MT-keyed and single-witness WLC.
findings.grounds: boundary_evidence_refs carries 'web:Isa.28.29 (setumah, single-witness)' and 'web:Isa.29.8 (setumah, single-witness)'. Both marks are real and correctly typed (pmarks_Isa.json marks: SAMEKH at Isa.28.29 and at Isa.29.8), and Isa 28-29 are identity chapters so the coordinates resolve, but the WEB witness carries no parashah layer and the campaign convention keys pmarks to oshb: refs. The batch's p07 rows cite the identical mark class under oshb:. The validator tolerates the form because it crosswalks web: refs to the MT key before lookup — the same MT-number-under-web-prefix shape that is a live hazard inside the offset zones.
findings.proposed_change: Re-prefix both entries as oshb:Isa.28.29 (setumah, single-witness) and oshb:Isa.29.8 (setumah, single-witness).

findings.claim: The English gloss at web:Isa.29.1 runs three Hebrew words past the splice it is paired with.
findings.grounds: The row pairs ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.29.1, byte tier) with 'Woe to Ariel! Ariel, the city where David encamped!' (web:Isa.29.1); 'the city where David encamped' renders קִרְיַ֖ת חָנָ֣ה דָוִ֑ד (oshb:Isa.29.1, byte tier), outside the splice. The WEB run is verbatim; the defect is extent parity only.
findings.proposed_change: Either extend the splice through קִרְיַ֖ת חָנָ֣ה דָוִ֑ד (oshb:Isa.29.1, byte tier) or cut the gloss to 'Woe to Ariel! Ariel'.

findings.claim: A chapter-break fact is carried inside the front-edge warrant without a non-evidential label.
findings.grounds: The opening sentence reads 'a fresh hoy onset after the chapter break at web:Isa.28.29'. The onset itself is a ruled tier-1 signal and is spliced — ה֚וֹי אֲרִיאֵ֣ל אֲרִיאֵ֔ל (oshb:Isa.29.1, byte tier) — so the tier-4 element is decorative rather than load-bearing, but it stands unlabelled inside the front-edge ground where the marker policy admits no tier-4 weight at all.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'after the chapter break at web:Isa.28.29' with 'after the doxological close at web:Isa.28.29', which names the text rather than the division.

findings.claim: The internal-cohesion bridge is quoted as two runs that do not match at the named skeleton tier, and carries no distribution digit.
findings.grounds: The rationale states that oshb:Isa.29.16 and oshb:Isa.29.17 'share the same verb form הַיֹּצֵ֖ר יֵֽחָשֵׁ֑ב (oshb:Isa.29.16, byte tier) / וְהַכַּרְמֶ֖ל לַיַּ֥עַר יֵחָשֵֽׁב (oshb:Isa.29.17, byte tier) at the consonantal-skeleton tier'. Each run collates byte tier in its own verse, but as quoted they share nothing at skeleton tier — one is two words, the other three, and only the final verb יֵחָשֵֽׁב (oshb:Isa.29.17, byte tier) is common. The tier choice is right for that verb (the oshb:Isa.29.16 form retains a meteg, which accent_stripped preserves, so skeleton is the lowest tier at which they agree), but the quoted extents do not let a reader check the claim. No digit is given for the bridge either, although the row supplies digits for its other catchword: the verb's skeleton stands at 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses — oshb:Isa.10.7, oshb:Isa.13.17, oshb:Isa.29.16, oshb:Isa.29.17, oshb:Isa.32.15). This is the row's stated load-bearing evidence for holding Isa.29.17-Isa.29.21 with the woe.
findings.proposed_change: Quote the shared verb alone on both sides at skeleton tier, keep the two context runs separately at byte tier, and add the 5-verse book-wide digit so the bridge's distinctiveness is on the record.

findings.claim: The '20 book-wide' scroll-noun digit is a bare substring count blending a place name, a different noun, and a verb family.
findings.grounds: device_notes gives 'the noun's skeleton standing at exactly 4 verses in Isa.28-31 ... and 20 book-wide'. The in-window figure re-derives exactly (4 verses: oshb:Isa.29.11, oshb:Isa.29.12, oshb:Isa.29.18, oshb:Isa.30.8, all the scroll noun). The 20-verse book-wide figure is the contiguous skeleton substring count and includes, at minimum, the number noun (oshb:Isa.10.19, oshb:Isa.21.17, oshb:Isa.40.26), the scribe noun (oshb:Isa.33.18, oshb:Isa.36.3), the recount verb (oshb:Isa.22.10, oshb:Isa.43.21), and the place name Sepharvaim (oshb:Isa.36.19, oshb:Isa.37.13) — none of them the noun the row names. The row does check the K/Q layer before slicing here and its disclosure is accurate: pmarks_Isa.json records 1 K/Q note at Isa.29.11, and the quoted הַסֵּ֣פֶר (oshb:Isa.29.11, byte tier) does stand before the doubled token pair later in that verse.
findings.proposed_change: Either restrict the book-wide digit to the scroll noun by sweeping its attested spellings and naming them, or drop the book-wide figure and keep the in-window 4-verse digit, which is sound.

findings.claim: The rear-edge warrant asserts a koh-amar frame at Isa.29.22 with no pointed splice, no oshb ref, and no frame owner named.
findings.grounds: The closing clause reads 'the verse just before the koh-amar address to the house of Jacob at web:Isa.29.22'; boundary_evidence_refs carries web:Isa.29.22 only. The verse's own bytes are לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.29.22, byte tier) — a divine frame, the tetragrammaton standing as the speaker — so the claim is true, but the row leaves its rear edge on the rendering and does not name whose frame it is, the discipline the divine-vs-royal-messenger split imposes on every koh-amar claim.
findings.proposed_change: Splice לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל בֵּ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב (oshb:Isa.29.22, byte tier) into the closing sentence, name it a divine frame, and add oshb:Isa.29.22 to boundary_evidence_refs.

findings.claim: Two parashah-mark claims are cited under a web: prefix, though the layer is MT-keyed and single-witness WLC.
findings.grounds: boundary_evidence_refs carries 'web:Isa.29.14 (setumah, single-witness)' and 'web:Isa.29.21 (setumah, single-witness)'. Both marks are real and correctly typed (pmarks_Isa.json marks: SAMEKH at Isa.29.14 and at Isa.29.21), and Isa 29 is an identity chapter so the coordinates resolve, but the WEB witness carries no parashah layer and the campaign convention keys pmarks to oshb: refs; the validator only passes them by crosswalking to the MT key first.
findings.proposed_change: Re-prefix both entries as oshb:Isa.29.14 (setumah, single-witness) and oshb:Isa.29.21 (setumah, single-witness).

findings.claim: The English gloss at web:Isa.29.15 runs one Hebrew word past the splice it is paired with.
findings.grounds: The row pairs ה֛וֹי הַמַּעֲמִיקִ֥ים מֵֽיהוָ֖ה לַסְתִּ֣ר (oshb:Isa.29.15, byte tier) with 'Woe to those who deeply hide their counsel from Yahweh' (web:Isa.29.15); 'their counsel' renders עֵצָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.29.15, byte tier), the word immediately after the splice. The WEB run is verbatim; the defect is extent parity only.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the splice by one word to include עֵצָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.29.15, byte tier), or cut the gloss to 'Woe to those who deeply hide ... from Yahweh'.
